mechanism: scripts/ledger.py fetched the frozen-fork null pool with a bare `kaggle competitions submissions`, which returns only the 50 most recent submissions. The null pool is defined by a description tag across the whole submission history, so as non-ledger submissions accumulate the oldest ledger members fall off the end of the window. The pool is therefore a SLIDING WINDOW that silently shrinks, and it sets the sealed mean-of-4 promotion bar for every arm in the campaign.
summary: On 2026-08-28 the ledger recomputed as n=35, mean 0.936, sd 0.181, bar 1.0975 against a record of n=37, 0.9316/0.1771, bar 1.089. Two members had been pushed out of the 50-row window by newer non-ledger draws. Fixed by paging at the CLI maximum (--page-size 200) plus a fail-closed guard that refuses to report any number when the fetch returns >= the page maximum, since truncation cannot then be ruled out. After the fix the ledger reproduces n=37, 0.9316/0.1771, bar 1.089 exactly.
lesson: A pool defined by a filter over ALL history must be fetched over all history; a paginated API default turns it into a sliding window that loses data in the direction of looking healthy (n stays plausible, the bar drifts up, and arms get rejected for it). The recurring campaign note that 'the bar drifts, always re-read runs/ledger.json' was partly this artifact rather than real movement. Guard the truncation, do not just raise the page size: a limit that is merely larger still fails silently on the day it is reached.
